title: HopcroftUllman-1979-AutomataTheoryLanguagesComputation
universal_lens: Automata theory unifies computation as state-transition systems over formal languages, where nondeterminism induces complexity hierarchies and grammar classes define recognizer expressiveness, establishing a lattice of decidability bounded by the Church-Turing thesis.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps language recognition to Bayesian model evidence: regular languages correspond to finite-memory conjugate priors, context-free to stack-augmented hierarchical priors, and recursively enumerable to unbounded computation; conformal prediction sets derive from automata acceptance boundaries.
gse_mapping: GSE treats game states as configurations in a pushdown automaton; play sequences form words in a context-free grammar; strategy synthesis reduces to parsing with attribute grammars; Nash equilibria correspond to fixed points in the transition monoid.

primitives.name: Nondeterministic Complexity Hierarchy Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: First has been the use of language-theory concepts, such as nondeterminism and the complexity hierarchies, to prove lower bounds on the inherent complexity of certain practical problems.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: NTIME(f(n)): nondeterministic time class (dimensionless); DTIME(f(n)): deterministic time class (dimensionless); SPACE(f(n)): space class (dimensionless); f: N -> N monotone resource bound
primitives.assumptions: Deterministic and nondeterministic Turing machines; time/space constructible functions; hierarchy theorems require f(n) >= n
primitives.breakdown_regime: Collapses when P = NP or when resource bounds are non-constructible; relativization barrier prevents resolution via diagonalization alone

layer2.mapping: GSI: Hypothesis class complexity maps to NTIME vs DTIME separation; conformal set size tracks certificate verification cost. GSE: Adversarial branching factor maps to nondeterministic choices; minimax depth maps to space hierarchy.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical: SAT solver runtime vs instance size; proof complexity lower bounds; conformal prediction interval width vs model class VC dimension

primitives.name: Grammar-Recognizer Duality Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Second has been the application of language-theory ideas, such as regular expressions and context-free grammars, in the design of software, such as compilers and text processors.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: G = (V, T, P, S): context-free grammar (dimensionless tuple); M = (Q, Sigma, Gamma, delta, q0, Z0, F): pushdown automaton (dimensionless tuple); L(G) = L(M): language equivalence (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Chomsky hierarchy containment: regular subset CFL subset CSL subset RE; parsing algorithms exist for LL(k), LR(k) grammars; ambiguity decidable for regular, undecidable for CFL
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inherent ambiguity in CFLs breaks unique parse tree assumption; LR(k) parsing fails for non-LR grammars; regular expressions cannot express nested structures

layer2.mapping: GSI: Grammar prior defines hypothesis space; recognizer implements posterior computation; parsing = Bayesian inference. GSE: Game grammar defines legal move sequences; recognizer validates play; attribute grammar computes payoffs.
layer2.telemetry: Parser generator conflict counts; ambiguity detection rates; compiler error recovery accuracy; conformal calibration error vs grammar complexity

primitives.name: Lower Bound Certificate Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: First has been the use of language-theory concepts, such as nondeterminism and the complexity hierarchies, to prove lower bounds on the inherent complexity of certain practical problems.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: L in NP: language with polynomial-time verifier (dimensionless); L in coNP: complement language (dimensionless); reduction: f: Sigma* -> Sigma* computable in logspace (dimensionless); hardness: L' <=_p L (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Cook-Levin theorem: SAT is NP-complete; polynomial hierarchy does not collapse; one-way functions exist for average-case hardness
primitives.breakdown_regime: Natural proofs barrier prevents circuit lower bounds; algebrization barrier extends relativization; fine-grained complexity requires stronger conjectures (SETH, OVH)

layer2.mapping: GSI: Lower bound = minimum description length of evidence; certificate = sufficient statistic. GSE: Lower bound = minimum search depth for forced win; certificate = winning strategy witness.
layer2.telemetry: Proof length in resolution/PCP systems; SAT solver clause database growth; endgame tablebase size vs position complexity

primitives.name: Automata-Theoretic Compilation Pipeline
primitives.verbatim_quote: USE OF THE BOOK Both authors have used Chapters 1 through 8 for a senior-level course, omitting only the material on inherent ambiguity in Chapter 4 and portions of Chapter 8.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Lexer: regex -> DFA (states: dimensionless); Parser: CFG -> PDA/LR(k) (stack depth: dimensionless); Semantic analysis: attribute grammar -> annotated AST (attributes: dimensionless); Codegen: IR -> target ISA (instructions: dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Source language is context-free; lexical syntax is regular; semantic rules are syntax-directed; target machine is Turing-complete
primitives.breakdown_regime: Context-sensitive syntax breaks CFG parsing; dependent types require theorem proving; JIT compilation introduces runtime feedback loops; quantum targets break classical ISA assumptions

layer2.mapping: GSI: Pipeline stages = successive Bayesian updates; lexer = sufficient statistic extraction; parser = structure learning; codegen = decision rule compilation. GSE: Lexer = move classification; parser = sequence validation; semantic analysis = position evaluation; codegen = move selection.
layer2.telemetry: Compilation time vs source size; optimization pass effectiveness; runtime performance vs static analysis precision; conformal coverage vs pipeline depth

The preface establishes two pillars: (1) nondeterminism and complexity hierarchies as tools for proving inherent lower bounds, and (2) regular expressions and context-free grammars as engineering primitives for compilers. These dualize as theory vs practice, proof vs construction. The nondeterministic hierarchy operator formalizes the first pillar: NTIME/DTIME separation creates a lattice of certificate verification costs. The grammar-recognizer duality formalizes the second: every grammar class has an equivalent automaton recognizer, with parsing as the computational bridge. The lower bound certificate operator extracts the proof-theoretic content: NP-completeness reduces lower bounds to reduction existence. The compilation pipeline operator sequences the engineering artifacts: regex->DFA, CFG->PDA, attributes->AST, IR->ISA. Failure modes align: hierarchy collapses (P=NP), inherent ambiguity (non-unique parse), natural proofs barrier (circuit lower bounds), context-sensitive syntax (CFG inadequacy). Each primitive maps to GSI/GSE via isomorphism (hierarchy<->evidence/complexity, lower bounds<->MDL/search depth) or derived kernel (grammar<->prior/posterior, pipeline<->Bayesian update sequence).
